receipt.public_excerpt: “The wall has been the topic du jour for the past few weeks,” Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang, whose company helps OpenAI, Meta, and others train their models, told the conference’s host, Eric Newcomer, during the morning’s first session. “Have we hit a wall? Yes and no.”

evidence_items.explanation: Wang publicly used the 'wall' framing on Nov 20, 2024, three days before the post. He partly agreed that a wall had been hit, and the report links it to diminishing returns from training.

receipt.public_excerpt: Google and others are starting to see diminishing returns from training their next models.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the diminishing-returns idea was in wide circulation across the industry in November 2024. The article's subhead says 'Everyone in AI seems to agree that new models are hitting a scaling wall.'

receipt.public_excerpt: “They’re kind of hitting the same ceiling on capabilities. Now there’s lots of smart people in the industry working to break through those ceilings, but sitting here today, if you just looked at the data, if you just looked at the charts of performance over time, what you would say is there’s at least a local topping out of capabilities that’s happening,” Andreessen continued.

evidence_items.explanation: Andreessen voiced the idea of diminishing returns, a ceiling and a topping out of capabilities, in podcast remarks reported Nov 6, 2024. He did not use the word 'wall'. The event date is the report's publication date; the remarks were made on or shortly before it.
